info.title: Insider Notification System API
info.description:
Event-driven notification service for **SMS**, **email** and **push**.

Notifications are accepted (`202`) and delivered asynchronously by queue
workers with per-channel rate limiting (100 messages/second), priorities
(`high`, `normal`, `low`), retries with exponential backoff and a circuit
breaker. Follow progress with `GET /notifications/{id}`, `GET /batches/{id}`
or in real time over WebSocket (Reverb, channels `notifications.{id}` and
`batches.{id}`, event `notification.status`).

**Idempotency** – send an `Idempotency-Key` header on create requests; batch
items can carry their own `idempotency_key`.

**Tracing** – every response carries `X-Correlation-ID`; send your own to
correlate logs end to end.

**Errors** – `422` validation errors list fields as `notifications.{index}.{field}`
for batches; `409` means the operation does not fit the notification's
current status (cancel, retry) or an idempotency key was reused with a
different payload.

get.description:
Newest first, cursor paginated (follow `links.next`). Multi-value
filters take a comma separated list, e.g. `?status=queued,retrying`.
`from` / `to` filter on the creation time.

next_cursor.description: The "cursor" that points to the next set of items.

post.description:
The notification is persisted and processed asynchronously; poll its
status with `GET /notifications/{id}`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header
to make retries safe: repeating a request with the same key returns the
original notification (200) instead of creating a new one (202).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated key returns the original notification (200) instead of creating a new one.

parameters.name: X-Correlation-ID
parameters.description: Optional trace ID (letters, digits, ".", "_", "-"; max 64). Generated when missing and echoed on every response.

recipient.description: E.164 phone number (sms), email address (email) or device token (push).

content.description: Message text. Required unless `template` is given. SMS: max 10 segments (GSM-7 1530 / UCS-2 670 characters); push: 1000; email: 100000.

template.description: Name of a template to render instead of `content`.

scheduled_at.description: Deliver later (ISO 8601, future, max 30 days ahead).

202.description: Accepted for delivery (or 200 when replayed from an Idempotency-Key).

post.description:
Only notifications that have not reached a worker yet can be cancelled
(scheduled, pending, queued, or waiting for a retry). Cancelling an
already cancelled notification succeeds. Otherwise responds with 409.

Re-queues a notification that ended in `failed` with a fresh retry
budget; its attempt history is kept. Responds with 409 for any other
status.

Accepts up to 1000 notifications. The whole request is validated first;
if any item is invalid nothing is created and the errors point at the
offending items (`notifications.{index}.{field}`).

Items may carry their own `idempotency_key`. Items whose key was already
used are not created again and are reported with `duplicate: true` and
the ID of the existing notification.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated key returns the original batch (200).

parameters.name: X-Correlation-ID
parameters.description: Optional trace ID, echoed on every response.

notifications.description: Up to 1000 notifications, each with the fields of `POST /notifications` plus an optional `idempotency_key`.

examples.content: Flash sale: 40% off for one hour!
Your order is on its way

202.description: Accepted for delivery (or 200 when replayed from an Idempotency-Key).

get.description:
Aggregated progress of the batch: how many notifications are in each
status. List the notifications themselves with
`GET /notifications?batch_id={id}`.

post.description:
Cancels every notification of the batch that is still cancellable.
Notifications already being processed or finished are not affected.

Re-queues every `failed` notification of the batch with a fresh retry
budget and reports how many were re-queued.

Use it when creating notifications with `"template": "<name>"` and

delete.description: Existing notifications keep their rendered content.

get.description:
Per channel, over a sliding window (`?window=` minutes, 1-60, default 5):
sent / failed counts, success and attempt failure rates, throughput,
provider and end-to-end latency percentiles, queue depth per priority
(pending, delayed, reserved, age of the oldest pending job) and the
circuit breaker state. Plus the number of notifications in each
non-final status.

`ok` / `degraded` answer 200 (the API is usable; `degraded` means
delivery is impaired: no workers or an open circuit). `down` answers
503 (PostgreSQL or Redis unreachable).

AttemptOutcome.description:
Result of a single delivery attempt against the provider. | | |---| | `success`
| | `retryable_failure`
Timeout, connection error, 5xx, 429 or malformed 2xx response. | | `permanent_failure`
Any other 4xx: retrying would produce the same result. |
AttemptOutcome.title: AttemptOutcome

NotificationStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a notification. Happy path: [scheduled →] pending → queued → processing → sent Retry: processing → retrying → processing → … Give up: processing → failed (permanent error / budget exhausted) Manual retry: failed → queued Recovery: processing | retrying → queued (stuck after a worker crash) Cancel: scheduled | pending | queued | retrying → cancelled | | |---| | `scheduled`
Waiting for its scheduled_at time. | | `pending`
Persisted, not yet handed to the queue. | | `queued`
Sitting in a queue, waiting for a worker. | | `processing`
Claimed by a worker; a provider call is in flight. | | `retrying`
Last attempt failed with a retryable error; waiting for its backoff. | | `sent`
Accepted by the provider. | | `failed`
Permanent error, or retry budget exhausted. | | `cancelled`
Cancelled by an API consumer before it was sent. |
